st.1: Sutkagendor on the Makran coast marks the western limit.

x: All three statements are correct: Sutkagendor (Makran coast) is the western limit, Alamgirpur (Hindon, Meerut) the eastern and Manda (Chenab) the northern.

st.1: The Harappans were the first to grow cotton, which the Egyptians called Sindon.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the name Sindon for Harappan cotton is Greek, not Egyptian. Statement 2 is wrong: maize, an American crop, was not grown by the Harappans.

st.1: Silver and tin were exported.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: silver and tin were imported, not exported. Statement 2 is wrong: woollens were not a Harappan export.

st.3: Toy carts with seated drivers come from Chanhudaro in Gujarat.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: terracottas were crude objects used by common people. Statement 3 is wrong: Chanhudaro, the source of the toy carts, is in Sindh, not Gujarat.

st.2: Moksha is a Rig Vedic Samhita term that the Upanishads only elaborated.
st.1: The doctrine of transmigration is first found in the Rig Veda.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: transmigration first appears in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad. Statement 2 is wrong: moksha is not a Samhita term and is first discussed in the Upanishads. Statement 3 is wrong: the Upanishads trace bondage and sorrow to ignorance, not to sacrifice.

st.1: The Barabar caves, which carry Ashokan inscriptions, are in Bihar.

x: All three statements are correct: the Barabar caves (Gaya, Bihar) carry Ashokan inscriptions, Nasik carries Gautami Balashri's inscription and Sittanavasal is a painted Jain cave shrine.

st.3: He died by Sallekhana at Pavapuri in Bihar.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the followers of Sthulabhadra, who stayed in the north, became the Svetambaras. Statement 3 is wrong: he died by Sallekhana at Shravanabelagola in Karnataka; Pavapuri is linked with Mahavira.

st.1: The 80-pillared hall was found at Bulandibagh.
st.4: The Mauryan remains were excavated by R.D. Banerji.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 80-pillared hall was found at Kumrahar. Statement 3 is wrong: Megasthenes said the palace surpassed those of Susa and Ecbatana; the Persepolis comparison is a modern one. Statement 4 is wrong: the remains were excavated by D.B. Spooner.

st.1: Skandagupta's gold coins show a bow and arrow, the Nandi standard and Lakshmi.
st.2: In Samudragupta's time governors became hereditary feudatories.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Skandagupta's archer coins carry the Garuda standard, not Nandi. Statement 2 is wrong: governors became hereditary feudatories under Skandagupta, not Samudragupta. Statement 3 is wrong: the peacock-feeding type belongs to Kumaragupta I.

st.3: Nettal denoted a rural tax paid in cash.
st.1: Vetti, Muttaiyal and Kudimai were land taxes.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Vetti, Muttaiyal and Kudimai were forced labour services. Statement 2 is wrong: Irai was the land tax. Statement 3 is wrong: Nettal was compulsory labour; the rural cash tax was Antarayam.

st.2: Tank irrigation was a minor feature of the Chola economy, unlike under Vijayanagara and the Kakatiyas.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Kallanai was built by the Sangam king Karikala. Statement 2 is wrong: tank irrigation was a major feature of the Chola economy, as under Vijayanagara and the Kakatiyas.

st.4: The Sharqi kingdom of Jaunpur was founded by Zafar Khan under the last Tughlaq.
st.3: Harihara and Bukka returned to Hinduism under Ramanujacharya; their settlement Anegondi grew into Vijayanagara.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Prataparudra II was captured in 1323 by Ulugh Khan (Muhammad bin Tughlaq). Statement 3 is wrong: their guide was Vidyaranya. Statement 4 is wrong: Jaunpur was founded by Malik Sarwar (Khwaja Jahan); Zafar Khan founded the Gujarat sultanate.

st.4: Sheikh Salim Chishti was the father of Abul Fazl and Faizi.
st.1: Birbal was killed in 1586 fighting the Uzbeks.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Birbal was killed in 1586 fighting the Yusufzai. Statement 3 is wrong: the Maktab Khana was set up at Fatehpur Sikri. Statement 4 is wrong: their father was Sheikh Mubarak.

st.1: Under the 1656 ahdnamas Bijapur and Golconda accepted Mughal suzerainty, tribute and Mughal arbitration.
st.3: The Mughal Deccan had four subas – Khandesh, Berar, Golconda and Daulatabad.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the ahdnamas date from 1636. Statement 2 is wrong: the Inqiyad Nama was accepted by Abdullah Qutb Shah. Statement 3 is wrong: the four subas were Khandesh, Berar, Telangana and Daulatabad; Golconda was not yet Mughal.

st.3: She was one of several Mughal consorts whose names appeared on coins and farmans.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Itimad-ud-Daulah's tomb is at Agra. Statement 3 is wrong: she was the only Mughal consort whose name appeared on coins and farmans.

st.1: Dara Shikoh was betrayed by Malik Jiwan of Dadar and buried in Akbar's tomb at Sikandra.
st.3: Shah Shuja, governor of Bengal, fled to Persia.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Dara was buried in Humayun's Tomb. Statement 2 is wrong: Murad Bakhsh was executed in 1661. Statement 3 is wrong: Shah Shuja fled to Arakan.

st.1: Andal was one of three women among the Alvars.
st.4: Sekkizhar wrote the Periya Puranam under the Chola king Rajaraja I.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Andal was the only woman among the Alvars. Statement 2 is wrong: Karaikkal Ammaiyar was a Nayanar (Shaiva) saint. Statement 4 is wrong: Sekkizhar wrote under Kulottunga II.

st.4: He held that dying at Kashi assured liberation.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Kabir was a householder and rejected renunciation. Statement 4 is wrong: Kabir rejected the belief in Kashi as a place of liberation (he chose to die at Maghar) and held that one God may be called Ram, Rahim, Allah or Hari.

st.4: The foundation stone of the Baba Guru Nanak International University was laid at Amritsar in 2019.
st.1: He was born in 1469 at Kartarpur in a Khatri family.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: he was born at Talwandi (Nankana Sahib); Kartarpur is where he settled and died. Statement 3 is wrong: the langar began at Kartarpur. Statement 4 is wrong: the foundation stone was laid at Nankana Sahib.

st.2: Khanderi and Sindhudurg are Giri Durgs that guarded the Ghat passes.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Khanderi and Sindhudurg are Jal Durgs (sea forts) guarding the Konkan. Statement 3 is wrong: Vishalgad is a hill fort.

st.4: The Dutch factory at Bheemunipatnam dates from 1606.
st.1: The first Dutch factory, at Machilipatnam (1605), was set up by Van der Haghen with the permission of Abdullah Qutb Shah.
st.3: Palakollu (1652) was a weaving centre of the Krishna delta.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the permission came from Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah. Statement 2 is wrong: Petapuli was a Krishna-delta weaving centre. Statement 3 is wrong: Palakollu was a Godavari weaving centre. Statement 4 is wrong: Bheemunipatnam dates from 1641.

st.3: The titles of the Carnatic Nawab and the Tanjore Raja were abolished in 1848.
st.2: In 1856 Dalhousie announced that Bahadur Shah's successors would lose the imperial title.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 1856 announcement was Canning's. Statement 3 is wrong: the titles were abolished in 1855. Statement 4 is wrong: Nana Saheb's adoptive father was Baji Rao II.

st.3: On 9 May 1857, 85 sepoys of the 3rd Native Cavalry at Ambala were sentenced to ten years' imprisonment.
st.1: Mangal Pandey of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry rose at Dum Dum on 29 March 1857.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Mangal Pandey rose at Barrackpore. Statement 3 is wrong: the 85 sepoys were at Meerut. Statement 4 is wrong: the rebels proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar.

st.3: S.N. Sen held that the so-called First National War of Independence was neither first, nor national, nor a war of independence.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the official centenary history 'Eighteen Fifty-Seven' was written by S.N. Sen. Statement 3 is wrong: that verdict is R.C. Majumdar's.

st.3: After it Chanda Sahib became Nawab and Muhammad Ali fled to Trichinopoly.

x: All three statements are correct: Ambur, near Vellore, opened the Second Carnatic War; Anwaruddin was killed; Chanda Sahib became Nawab and Muhammad Ali fled to Trichinopoly.

st.1: He was Nawab twice – 1757-1760 and 1765-1767.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: his terms were 1757-1760 and 1763-1765 (he died in 1765). Statement 3 is wrong: Chinsura (Bidara) followed his intrigue with the Dutch.

st.1: He was the son-in-law of Mir Jafar and was placed on the throne by Clive in 1760.
st.2: Before becoming Nawab he was the Naib Nazim of Bihar.
st.3: His army was reorganised on European lines by the Frenchman Raymond.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: he was placed on the throne by Vansittart. Statement 2 is wrong: he was Faujdar of Purnia and Rangpur. Statement 3 is wrong: the Armenian Gurgin Khan reorganised his army; Raymond served the Nizam. Statement 4 is wrong: his gun factory was at Monghyr.

st.2: Reza Khan was naib diwan for Bengal and Raja Shitab Rai for Bihar.

x: All three statements are correct: the Company held the Diwani, Reza Khan and Shitab Rai were naib diwans for Bengal and Bihar, and the 1770 famine came under Cartier.

st.3: The Russell Brigade was raised by Resident Henry Russell.

x: All three statements are correct: after Kharda the Nizam turned to Raymond's French battalions, and the Russell Brigade was raised by Resident Henry Russell.

st.2: He served three Nizams, the last being Mir Mahbub Ali Khan.

x: All three statements are correct: Salar Jung I became Diwan in 1853, served three Nizams (Nasir-ud-Daula, Afzal-ud-Daula, Mahbub Ali Khan) and introduced the Zillabandi system.

st.1: Lord Lawrence's Resolution of 1870 was the first step towards financial decentralisation.
st.4: Lord Lytton's Resolution of 1882 is called the 'Magna Carta' of local self-government.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 1870 Resolution was Lord Mayo's. Statement 3 is wrong: under the 1919 Act local self-government was a transferred subject. Statement 4 is wrong: the 1882 Resolution was Lord Ripon's.

st.3: The Sri Bagh Pact of 16 November 1937 was concluded at the house of Kasinadhuni Nageswara Rao.

x: All three statements are correct: the People's Party was routed, Rajaji's Hindi move provoked Periyar, and the Sri Bagh Pact was signed at Kasinadhuni Nageswara Rao's house.

st.1: 'The Problem of the Rupee' was his Columbia doctoral thesis, accepted in 1923.
st.4: He was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1991.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: 'The Problem of the Rupee' was his LSE thesis. Statement 3 is wrong: his 1953 D.Litt came from Osmania University. Statement 4 is wrong: the Bharat Ratna came in 1990.

st.2: Jiddu Krishnamurti, born at Madanapalle in 1895, was identified by C.W. Leadbeater in 1909.

x: All three statements are correct: the Society was founded in New York (1875) and moved to Adyar (1882); Krishnamurti was spotted by Leadbeater in 1909 and left the Society in 1929.

st.1: It means the monk's renunciation of all wealth.

x: Neither statement is correct: 'Daridra Narayana' means God manifest in the poor, so serving the poor is serving God; it has nothing to do with renunciation of wealth or rebirth.

st.1: It was founded in 1878.

x: Neither statement is correct: Amrita Bazar Patrika was founded in 1868, and it turned into an English paper overnight in 1878, not 1881, to escape the Vernacular Press Act.

st.3: Women took part in it in large numbers for the first time.

x: All three statements are correct: the CDM was the first mass law-breaking movement, drew in the NWFP through the Khudai Khidmatgars and was the first movement with mass participation of women.

st.2: Arrival of the Simon Commission
st.4: First Round Table Conference

x: The correct order is 2-3-1-4: arrival of the Simon Commission (February 1928), Purna Swaraj resolution at Lahore (December 1929), Dandi March (March 1930), First Round Table Conference (November 1930).

st.1: The Axis powers were Germany, Italy and Japan, while China stayed neutral.
st.2: The war-crimes trials were held at Versailles in 1945-46.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: China fought with the Allies. Statement 2 is wrong: the trials were held at Nuremberg. Statement 3 is wrong: the 6 August bomb fell on Hiroshima; Nagasaki was bombed on 9 August.

st.1: He fled to Germany in 1915 after the Hardinge bomb case.
st.3: The call 'Avenge the blood of Indian Martyrs… Stand up against the entire Anglo-American enemy' is attributed to Mohan Singh.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: he fled to Japan. Statement 2 is wrong: he died in January 1945 and was never tried at the Red Fort. Statement 3 is wrong: the call is attributed to Rash Behari Bose.

st.2: The United Bengal plan of Sarat Chandra Bose and H.S. Suhrawardy was rejected by both the Congress and the Muslim League.

x: All three statements are correct: Plan Balkan was dropped after Nehru's reaction, the United Bengal plan was rejected by both Congress and the League, and V.P. Menon proposed early transfer on dominion status.

st.4: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
st.3: Mahatma Gandhi

x: The correct match is A-3, B-1, C-2, D-4: 'Sedition has become my religion' – Gandhi; Dandi compared to Napoleon's return from Elba – Subhas Chandra Bose; 'Generations to come…' – Albert Einstein; 'Swaraj is my birthright' – Tilak.

st.1: Pondicherry, Karikal, Mahe and Yanam passed to India de facto on 1 November 1956, after the Kizhur referendum.
st.2: Their de jure transfer took place on 16 August 1966.
st.4: Yanam, in the Krishna delta, is part of Puducherry UT.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the de facto transfer was on 1 November 1954. Statement 2 is wrong: the de jure transfer was on 16 August 1962. Statement 3 is wrong: Chandernagore merged into West Bengal. Statement 4 is wrong: Yanam lies in the Godavari delta.

st.2: Its last Nizam, Mir Osman Ali Khan, was the sixth Nizam.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Mir Osman Ali Khan was the seventh Nizam. Statement 3 is wrong: the Standstill Agreement kept existing arrangements for one year.

st.2: The AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1982 also covered Jogini, Basivi and Matangi dedication.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the AP Devadasis Act dates from 1988. Statement 3 is wrong: the Dubagunta anti-arrack movement began in Nellore district.

st.2: Kalluri Subba Rao signed it as a Rayalaseema leader.

x: All three statements are correct: the pact sought to allay Rayalaseema's fears, Kalluri Subba Rao signed for Rayalaseema, and in 1953 the capital went to Kurnool and the High Court to Guntur.

st.3: The Visalandhra idea of 1937 began in the Circar districts.

x: All three statements are correct: the Belgaum dispute continued, Prakasam earned 'Andhra Kesari' during the Simon boycott, and the 1937 Visalandhra idea began in the Circar districts.

st.1: Its members were Fazl Ali, H.N. Kunzru and Harishchandra Heda.
st.4: It recommended that Raichur and Gulbarga go to Bombay.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the third member was K.M. Panikkar, not Harishchandra Heda. Statement 3 is wrong: the merger needed a two-thirds majority. Statement 4 is wrong: Raichur and Gulbarga were to go to Mysore.

st.2: It was announced during the Jai Telangana agitation.

x: All three statements are correct: Indira Gandhi announced the Eight-Point Formula on 11 April 1969 during the Jai Telangana agitation, with a six-monthly review of Telangana's development.

st.2: Giddaluru, Dornala and Yerragondapalem are in Prakasam district.

x: All three statements are correct: Jwalapuram (Kurnool) is Upper Palaeolithic, Giddaluru, Dornala and Yerragondapalem are in Prakasam, and Nagarjunakonda spans the Palaeolithic to the Megalithic.

st.4: Telugu became the official language of AP in 1956.
st.1: The Desi bhasha of the common people belonged to the Indo-Aryan family.
st.2: The phrase 'Italian of the East', from Marco Polo, was used for Telugu by the British.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Desi bhasha was Dravidian. Statement 2 is wrong: the phrase comes from Niccolo de Conti. Statement 3 is wrong: the Telugu script grew out of Brahmi. Statement 4 is wrong: Telugu became the official language in 1966.

st.1: The Samayasara was written by Kundakundacharya, a Svetambara monk.
st.3: Jain tradition says Ashoka's grandson Dasaratha spread Jainism in Andhra.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Kundakundacharya was a Digambara monk. Statement 2 is wrong: Konakondla is in Anantapur district. Statement 3 is wrong: Jain tradition credits Samprati.

st.1: It was issued by Narasimhavarman I.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the inscription is Mahendravarman I's. Statement 3 is wrong: it claims the shrine was made without brick, timber, metal or mortar – it is cut in stone.

st.2: Pandaranga, one of his four Brahmin generals, built Pandurangapuram and a Maheswara temple on Kolleru lake.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Maheswara temple was on Pulicat lake. Statement 3 is wrong: the Addanki inscription is in the Taruvoja metre.

st.2: Alauddin Bahman Shah built the Gulbarga Jama Masjid, compared to the mosque of Cordoba.
st.3: Firuz Shah, the scholar-king, built an observatory near Bidar.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Gulbarga Jama Masjid was built under Muhammad Shah I. Statement 3 is wrong: Firuz Shah's observatory was near Daulatabad. Statement 4 is wrong: the kingdom ended in 1527.

st.4: The Gol Gumbaz, with its whispering gallery, is the tomb of Yusuf Adil Shah.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Krishnadevaraya defeated Ismail Adil Shah at Raichur. Statement 4 is wrong: the Gol Gumbaz is the tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah.

st.2: Bukka I was the first Vijayanagara king to use cannon.

x: All three statements are correct: the Dalavayi's standing army was paid every four months, Bukka I first used cannon, and horses came in through Goa, Honnavar and Bhatkal.

st.4: Sevappa Nayaka founded the Gingee kingdom under Achyutaraya.
st.1: Krishnappa Nayaka got Madurai after capturing his rebel father Nagama.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: it was Vishwanatha Nayaka who captured his father Nagama. Statement 2 is wrong: the Tirumala Rayala Mahal was built by Tirumala Nayaka. Statement 4 is wrong: Sevappa founded the Tanjore kingdom.

st.2: Its builders were governors of Penukonda.

x: All three statements are correct: Lepakshi is in Sri Sathya Sai district and was built c. 1530-40 under Achyutaraya by the Penukonda governors Virupanna and Veeranna.

st.1: Narasapuram, the chief shipbuilding centre of the 16th-17th centuries, is in Krishna district.
st.2: Tavernier described large, strongly built ships at Narasapuram under the Qutb Shahis.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Narasapuram is in West Godavari district. Statement 2 is wrong: the description is Methold's. Statement 3 is wrong: odaberam were sea-going ships.

st.1: Sullivan, First Member of the Board of Revenue, was appointed to inquire into its causes.

x: All three statements are correct: Sullivan inquired into the causes (Rutherford belongs to the 1922-24 rising), which were the mansabdar, the toddy tax and podu limits; the rebels were chiefly Koyas.

st.3: Eluru was known for its carpets and Kurnool for its blankets.

x: All three statements are correct: duty-free British cloth ruined the weavers, Visakhapatnam's exports fell from about Rs 7 lakh to Rs 1 lakh, and Eluru carpets and Kurnool blankets declined.

st.3: 256 Andhra delegates attended the Bombay session of 1915.
st.1: The first session of the INC (1885) welcomed the annexation of Upper Burma.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 1885 session opposed the annexation of Upper Burma. Statement 3 is wrong: the 256 Andhra delegates attended the Madras session of 1914. Statement 4 is wrong: the session demanded a cut in military expenditure.

st.3: He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 1981.
st.4: He formed the Swatantra Party in 1951.
st.1: He was born at Nidubrolu in Guntur district in 1910.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: he was born in 1900. Statement 2 is wrong: the minimum-wages memorandum to the Simon Commission is not his. Statement 3 is wrong: the Padma Vibhushan came in 1991. Statement 4 is wrong: in 1951 he formed the Krishikar Lok Party; the Swatantra Party came in 1959.

st.4: She was given the title "Desoddharaka".

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: after Chollangi she was sent to the Nellore jail. Statement 4 is wrong: her title was 'Desabandhavi'; 'Desoddharaka' was Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.

st.3: Mutnuri Krishna Rao edited it from 1907 until his death in 1945.

x: All three statements are correct: Krishna Patrika was founded in 1902 at Machilipatnam by Konda Venkatappayya and Dasu Narayana Rao, and Mutnuri Krishna Rao edited it from 1907 to 1945.

st.3: The Kuppam Bharani library ran mobile library boats.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 1919 conference was held at Madras. Statement 3 is wrong: the Kuppam Bharani library ran mobile library carts, not boats.

st.3: The Draft Constitution it published in February 1948 had 315 Articles and 8 Schedules.

x: All three statements are correct: the seven-member committee was set up on 29 August 1947, sat for 141 days and published a draft of 315 Articles and 8 Schedules.

st.1: The Battle of Ten Kings, described in the Rigveda, was fought by Sudas near the Vipas (Beas).

x: Neither statement is correct: the Battle of Ten Kings was fought on the Parushni (Ravi), and the Kalinga War was fought in c. 261 BC.

st.3: Patanjali's Mahabhashya is a commentary on Panini's Ashtadhyayi.

x: All three statements are correct: Malavikagnimitram is Kalidasa's first five-act play, Patanjali was Pushyamitra's priest, and the Mahabhashya comments on Panini.

st.1: Vatsaraja defeated Dharmapala at Monghyr.

x: Neither statement is correct: it was Nagabhata II who defeated Dharmapala at Monghyr, and Nagabhata II was a Pratihara, not a Pala.

st.1: Sulaiman called the Pala kingdom Juzr (Al-Juzr).

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Juzr was Sulaiman's name for the Pratihara kingdom. Statement 2 is wrong: Balhara was the Arab name for the Rashtrakuta king.

st.2: The Rashtrakutas declined by the late tenth century under Pala and Pratihara pressure.

x: Neither statement is correct: the Rashtrakuta age raised Kannada, not Telugu, to a classical medium, and the dynasty fell in the late tenth century to Chalukya and Chola pressure.

st.2: Mahabalipuram is called Mamallapuram after his father Mahendravarman I.
st.1: He bore the titles Mamalla ('great wrestler') and Gunabhara.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: his titles were Mamalla and Vatapikonda; Gunabhara was Mahendravarman I's. Statement 2 is wrong: Mamallapuram is named after Narasimhavarman I himself. Statement 3 is wrong: Vichitrachitta was Mahendravarman I's title.

st.4: The man's earring in the left ear and the woman's in the right signify the fusion of male and female principles.
st.3: In the Nataraja, the upper right hand in abhaya mudra signifies protection.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: bronzes were cast in South India before the Cholas, under the Pallavas. Statement 3 is wrong: the abhaya hand is the lower right; the upper right holds the damaru. Statement 4 is wrong: the man's earring is in the right ear and the woman's in the left.

st.1: Singhana II, the founder of the independent Yadava kingdom, took the title Teluguraya Sthapanacharya.
st.3: Jaitugi's killing of the Kakatiya Rudradeva is confirmed by the Motupalli inscription of Ganapatideva.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the founder was Bhillama V; Singhana II was the greatest Yadava. Statement 3 is wrong: the confirmation is the Paithan copper plate of Ramachandra. Statement 4 is wrong: Ganapatideva was freed as a counterweight to the Hoysala Veera Ballala II in the Krishna–Tungabhadra region.

st.4: In neolocal residence the couple lives with the husband's family.
st.1: The family is a secondary social institution, though it is the child's first school.
st.2: Durkheim defined the family by common residence, economic co-operation and reproduction.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the family is the basic, primary institution. Statement 2 is wrong: that definition is Murdock's. Statement 3 is wrong: in duolocal residence each spouse stays in his or her natal home (either or both alternately is bilocal). Statement 4 is wrong: neolocal means a new home; living with the husband's family is patrilocal.

st.1: Under Section 3(f), the sapinda relationship extends to three generations on the mother's side and five on the father's.

x: All three statements are correct: sapinda extends three generations through the mother and five through the father, Section 5(v) bars sapinda marriages unless custom allows, and the Delhi High Court upheld it in January 2024.

st.1: It does not apply to Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs.

x: Neither statement is correct: the Act does apply to Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs, and it does not apply to Scheduled Tribes unless the Central Government notifies otherwise.

st.2: Moiety
st.4: Phratry

x: The correct order from smallest to largest is 3-1-4-2: lineage, clan, phratry, moiety.

st.1: The kamin is the landholding patron caste, and the jajmans are the castes rendering hereditary services.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the jajman is the landholding patron and the kamins render the hereditary services. Statement 2 is wrong: kamins were paid mainly in kind, at harvest, not in monthly cash wages.

st.2: Mizoram became a State in 1987, a year after the Mizo Accord.

x: All three statements are correct: Nagaland was inaugurated on 1 December 1963, Mizoram became a State in 1987 after the 1986 Mizo Accord, and the DGHC (1988) was followed by the GTA (2012).

st.1: After the 2008 delimitation, 84 Lok Sabha seats are reserved for SCs and 47 for STs.

x: All three statements are correct: 84 SC and 47 ST Lok Sabha seats after the 2008 delimitation; Andhra Pradesh has 4 SC and 1 ST Lok Sabha seats and 29 SC and 7 ST Assembly seats.

st.3: The National Foundation for Communal Harmony mainly gives compensation to adult victims of communal violence.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 2011 Communal Violence Bill was never passed. Statement 3 is wrong: the Foundation mainly helps child victims of communal violence.

st.2: It is run by the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

x: All three statements are correct: the NCLP began in 1988 under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, and its Special Training Centres serve rescued children aged 9-14.

st.3: As per the PLFS 2025 annual report, India's youth (15-29) unemployment rate was 9.9%, higher in rural than in urban areas.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: adolescents (10-19) numbered about 253 million. Statement 3 is wrong: youth unemployment was higher in urban areas (13.6%) than rural (8.3%).

st.1: As per NFHS-5, 26.8% of women aged 20–24 were married before 18.
st.4: ALIVA, a data-driven model to end child marriage, was developed in Koraput district, Odisha.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the NFHS-5 figure is 23.3%. Statement 2 is wrong: West Bengal has the highest share. Statement 4 is wrong: ALIVA was developed in Nayagarh district.

st.4: Its cost is shared between the Centre and the States in the ratio 75:25.
st.3: It was renamed PM POSHAN (Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman) in 2019.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Tamil Nadu was the first State to introduce the mid-day meal. Statement 3 is wrong: it was renamed PM POSHAN in 2021. Statement 4 is wrong: the cost is shared 60:40.

st.4: One Nation One Ration Card lets migrants draw PDS ration only in their home State.
st.3: The migrant worker provisions of the OSH Code apply from 20 workers.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 1979 Act is subsumed in the OSH Code, 2020. Statement 3 is wrong: the OSH Code's migrant provisions apply from 10 workers. Statement 4 is wrong: ONORC lets migrants draw ration anywhere in India.

st.1: Press Note 3 (2020) requires government approval for FDI from countries sharing a land border with India.

x: All three statements are correct: Press Note 3 put FDI from land-border countries on the government route, the app bans used Section 69A of the IT Act, and the Strategic Economic Dialogue began in 2010.

st.3: It does not provide political-risk guarantees to foreign investors, which is MIGA's role.

x: All three statements are correct: the IMF gives short-term BoP support, not project finance; its Rapid Credit Facility serves low-income members; and political-risk guarantees come from MIGA, not the IMF.

st.3: Afghanistan joined in 2007 as its eighth member.

x: All three statements are correct: the SAARC Charter was signed at Dhaka on 8 December 1985, the Secretariat is at Kathmandu, and Afghanistan joined in 2007.

st.3: The Contingent Reserve Arrangement, a $100 billion liquidity pool, is a BRICS initiative.

x: All three statements are correct: the New Delhi Declaration sought IMF and World Bank quota reform, the NDB is headquartered at Shanghai, and the $100 billion CRA is a BRICS pool.

st.3: The Amending Act of 1781 (Act of Settlement) separated the judicial and executive functions.

x: All three statements are correct: the Governor-General had a four-member Council, the Supreme Court had Impey and three judges, and the 1781 Act of Settlement separated judicial and executive functions.

st.1: It took 2 years, 10 months and 18 days to frame the Constitution.

x: Neither statement is correct: the Assembly took 2 years, 11 months and 18 days and sat for 165 days; 141 days is the Drafting Committee's figure.

st.1: Under Article 371A, Parliament's laws on Naga customary law and land apply to Nagaland only if its Governor so directs.
st.3: Article 371F protects Mizo religious and social practices and customary law.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: under Article 371A such laws apply only if the Nagaland Legislative Assembly so resolves, not the Governor. Statement 3 is wrong: the Mizo protection is in Article 371G; 371F concerns Sikkim.

st.2: Under it, adolescents aged 15–18 are barred from hazardous work.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: adolescents are those aged 14–18. Statement 4 is wrong: the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act was passed in 1976.

st.2: 'Equal protection of the laws' is of American origin and is a negative concept.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: equal protection of the laws is a positive concept. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 14 permits reasonable classification but forbids class legislation.

st.3: The right to marry a person of one's choice was upheld in Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978).
st.1: Its protection is available only to citizens.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Article 21 protects citizens and non-citizens alike. Statement 3 is wrong: the right to marry a person of one's choice was upheld in Lata Singh v. State of UP (2006). Statement 4 is wrong: Supriyo Chakraborty held there is no unqualified fundamental right to marry.

st.1: The freedoms under Article 19 are available to citizens and foreigners alike.
st.3: Article 21A was inserted by the 93rd Amendment, 2005.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Article 19 freedoms are for citizens only. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 21A was inserted by the 86th Amendment, 2002. Statement 4 is wrong: Article 24 bars children below 14.

st.4: A Minister can be a member of it.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: it is not a financial committee. Statement 4 is wrong: a Minister cannot be a member of it.

st.1: It has 10 members from the Lok Sabha and 20 from the Rajya Sabha.

x: Neither statement is correct: the Committee has 20 Lok Sabha and 10 Rajya Sabha members, and a Minister cannot be a member.

st.3: The election can be challenged because of vacancies in the electoral college.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: acts done by the President before the election is declared void remain valid. Statement 3 is wrong: the election cannot be challenged on the ground of vacancies in the electoral college.

st.2: Executive-legislature deadlock is a demerit of the presidential system, not of the parliamentary system.

x: All three statements are correct: cabinet dictatorship is a parliamentary demerit, deadlock belongs to the presidential system, and the Assembly knew parliamentary government from the 1919 and 1935 Acts.

st.3: Lok Adalats can settle compoundable criminal matters and matrimonial disputes, but not divorce.

x: All three statements are correct: Lok Adalats take pending and pre-litigation cases, about 55% of lower-court cases were over two years old (NJDG 2017), and Lok Adalats settle compoundable and matrimonial matters but not divorce.

st.2: Telangana was removed from its jurisdiction in 2020.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Telangana was removed in 2016; 2020 is the year APAT was abolished. Statement 3 is wrong: its cases went to the AP High Court, not the CAT.

st.1: Sikkim was added to it in 1998.
st.2: Since 2018 the Union Minister of DoNER is its ex-officio chairman.

x: Neither statement is correct: Sikkim was added to the NEC in 2002, and since 2018 the Union Home Minister is its ex-officio chairman (the DoNER Minister is vice-chairman).

st.1: The net proceeds of taxes under Article 269 that are assigned to the States form part of the Consolidated Fund of India.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Article 269 proceeds assigned to the States do not form part of the Consolidated Fund of India. Statement 4 is wrong: the Article 270 divisible pool excludes surcharges and cesses.

st.2: Approval of the borrowing limits of the States under Article 293
st.3: Measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of India to supplement the resources of Panchayats and Municipalities
st.1: Allocation of funds among the States under Centrally Sponsored Schemes

x: None of these is a Finance Commission function under Article 280(3). It recommends the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes and their allocation among States, the principles of grants-in-aid, and measures to augment a State's (not India's) Consolidated Fund for local bodies; State borrowing consent under Article 293 lies with the Union Government, scheme funds with the ministries, and GST rates with the GST Council.

st.3: The Commission has been a multi-member body continuously since 1 October 1993.

x: All three statements are correct: two Election Commissioners were first added on 16 October 1989, the posts were abolished in January 1990, and the Commission has been multi-member since 1 October 1993.

st.2: The 42nd Amendment gave constitutional status to a joint National Commission for SCs and STs.
st.1: Before the 103rd Amendment, the NCBC was a statutory body under a 1993 Act.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: NCBC got constitutional status by the 102nd Amendment. Statement 2 is wrong: the joint commission came from the 65th Amendment. Statement 3 is wrong: the split came with the 89th Amendment, 2003.

st.2: It may intervene in court proceedings involving human-rights allegations even without the court's approval.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it may intervene only with the court's approval. Statement 4 is wrong: it cannot inquire into a complaint solely against a private individual.

st.1: Anna Hazare of India Against Corruption fasted at Ramlila Maidan in April 2011 and at Jantar Mantar in August 2011.

x: Neither statement is correct: Anna Hazare fasted at Jantar Mantar in April and at Ramlila Maidan in August 2011, and the Joint Drafting Committee's co-chairman was Shanti Bhushan.

st.3: Praveen Kumar Srivastava became the acting Central Vigilance Commissioner from 3 August 2026.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the selection committee is the PM, the Union Home Minister and the Leader of the Opposition. Statement 3 is wrong: A.S. Rajeev became acting CVC from 3 August 2026, after Praveen Kumar Srivastava's term ended.

st.1: At least two-thirds of its members must be judicial members.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: at least 50% must be judicial members. Statement 3 is wrong: the Cabinet Secretary is not on the selection committee (PM, Speaker, LoP, CJI and an eminent jurist).

st.3: Registered-unrecognised parties number over 2,800, and nearly all of them contested the 2024 general election.
st.1: The original Constitution regulated political parties in Part XV on elections.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the original Constitution had no provision on parties. Statement 2 is wrong: the Tenth Schedule came with the 52nd Amendment, 1985. Statement 3 is wrong: only about 750 of the 2,800-plus RUPPs contested in 2024.

st.2: Kerala's People's Plan Campaign, launched on 17 August 1996, devolved about 35-40% of plan funds to local bodies.

x: All three statements are correct: the DPC is a constitutional body under Article 243ZD, Kerala's 1996 campaign devolved about 35-40% of plan funds, and SabhaSaar is an AI tool for Gram Sabha minutes.

st.2: It came into force on 1 January 2009.
st.4: It does not override other laws inconsistent with it.
st.1: It was passed by the Rajya Sabha on 15 December and the Lok Sabha on 18 December 2006.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Lok Sabha passed it on 15 December and the Rajya Sabha on 18 December 2006. Statement 2 is wrong: it came into force on 31 December 2007. Statement 3 is wrong: the nodal Ministry is Tribal Affairs. Statement 4 is wrong: it overrides inconsistent laws.

st.3: It is now known as SCSP.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Tribal Sub-Plan was adopted in the Fifth Plan. Statement 3 is wrong: it is now DAPST; SCSP is the Scheduled Caste Sub-Plan.

st.2: In July 2026 PNGRB approved 25 Geographical Areas in Andhra Pradesh for City Gas Distribution.
st.1: CERC regulates City Gas Distribution networks.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: City Gas Distribution is regulated by PNGRB, not CERC. Statement 2 is wrong: 10 Geographical Areas were approved. Statement 3 is wrong: East Godavari has the most connections.

st.1: It was set up in 2011 under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: FSSAI was set up in 2008. Statement 2 is wrong: it works under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, not the DGHS.

st.2: The NCLAT has heard appeals against the National Financial Reporting Authority since 7 May 2018.

x: All three statements are correct: APTEL was set up on 24 August 2004, NCLAT has heard NFRA appeals since 7 May 2018, and L. Chandra Kumar made High Court review of tribunals part of the basic structure.

st.4: It may bar an endorser for up to five years for a repeat offence.
st.2: It can order recalls and refunds but cannot file class-action complaints.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the CCPA can file class-action complaints as well as order recalls and refunds. Statement 3 is wrong: the first-offence penalty is up to Rs 10 lakh. Statement 4 is wrong: a repeat offender can be barred for up to three years.

st.4: The CCPA fined Meta Rs 50 lakh over walkie-talkie listings.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the drug-eluting stent cap was cut from Rs 29,600 to Rs 27,890. Statement 4 is wrong: the CCPA fined Meta Rs 10 lakh.

st.3: The first Voice of Global South Summit was held in January 2023.

x: All three statements are correct: the 2026 New Delhi Declaration backed UN reform, the India-UK CETA was signed in July 2025, and the first Voice of Global South Summit was held in January 2023.

st.1: The Right Canal of Nagarjuna Sagar is the Telugu Ganga Canal.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Right Canal is the Jawahar Canal. Statement 3 is wrong: Lakhwar is on the Yamuna, not the Ganga.

st.2: It retained most of the coastline, but the Machilipatnam port went to Telangana.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: residual AP kept the entire coastline and all ports, leaving Telangana landlocked. Statement 4 is wrong: AP has about 29% of India's fish and about 75% of cultured-shrimp exports.

st.3: It is the second WTO agreement with an environmental-sustainability objective, after the Trade Facilitation Agreement.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it covers marine wild-capture fishing, not aquaculture or inland fishing. Statement 3 is wrong: it is the first WTO agreement with an environmental-sustainability objective; the Trade Facilitation Agreement has none.

st.2: In that paper Uttar Pradesh recorded the largest fall in the number of poor (5.94 crore).

x: All three statements are correct: multidimensional poverty fell from 29.17% to 11.28% (24.82 crore people), Uttar Pradesh had the largest fall (5.94 crore), and the 2020 package included free foodgrains.

st.1: Its population was 495.77 lakh and its sex ratio 993.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the sex ratio of residual AP was 997. Statement 2 is wrong: decadal growth in 2001-11 was 9.21%.

st.3: Nearly 70% of elderly women lack a formal pension, compared with about 40% of elderly men.

x: All three statements are correct: the elderly are 9.7% (SRS 2024), about 230 million by 2036, and nearly 70% of elderly women, against about 40% of men, lack a formal pension.

st.1: Visakhapatnam was to be the judicial seat.
st.3: In the South African model it cited, Pretoria is the legislative and Bloemfontein the judicial capital.
st.4: It was to be enacted through the AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development Bill and the APCRDA (Repeal) Bill, 2019.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Kurnool was to be the judicial seat (Visakhapatnam the executive). Statement 2 is wrong: it rested on the G.N. Rao Committee and a Boston Consulting Group study. Statement 3 is wrong: Cape Town is the legislative capital (Pretoria the executive). Statement 4 is wrong: the two Bills were of 2020.

st.3: Bharat Nirman was launched after SGSY.

x: All three statements are correct: the CDP (1952) came before Food for Work (1977-78), SGSY began in 1999, and Bharat Nirman (2005) came after it.

st.1: India's total fertility rate of 2.2 is above the replacement level of 2.1.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: India's TFR is 1.9, below replacement. Statement 2 is wrong: the demographic dividend is expected to peak around 2030.

st.3: Sen holds that public spending on health and education should get priority, as it also drives growth.

x: All three statements are correct: 'Why Growth Matters' is by Bhagwati and Panagariya, 'An Uncertain Glory' by Sen and Dreze, and Sen gives priority to health and education.

st.3: The Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (1989) was formed by merging IRDP and TRYSEM.
st.1: The Ninth Plan was the first to set monitorable targets.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Tenth Plan first set monitorable targets. Statement 2 is wrong: NHM and NRHM were launched in 2005, during the Tenth Plan. Statement 3 is wrong: JRY merged NREP and RLEGP.

st.2: Industry grew 7.26% against a target of 12%.
st.1: It targeted 9% GSDP growth and achieved about 5.28%.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: AP's target was 9.5% (9% was the national target). Statement 2 is wrong: the industry target was 10%. Statement 4 is wrong: the social sector, not industry, got first priority.

st.2: Planning is not a constitutional requirement in India; economic and social planning is only a Concurrent List entry.

x: All three statements are correct: post-1991 planning is indicative, planning is not mandated by the Constitution, and the Planning Commission's abolition ended discretionary plan grants.

st.3: The IRDA Act was passed in 2000.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2025 Act raised the insurance FDI cap from 74% to 100%. Statement 3 is wrong: the IRDA Act was passed in 1999.

st.2: The southern States welcomed the population base it was asked to use.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: its terms mandated the 2011 Census. Statement 2 is wrong: the southern States objected to the 2011 base.

st.3: Its recommendations are advisory and not binding on the Union.

x: All three statements are correct: the President constitutes the Finance Commission every five years with a Chairman and four members, and its recommendations are only advisory.

st.3: Rents and user charges such as payments for municipal water supply are non-tax revenue.

x: All three statements are correct: property tax is the main own tax, professional tax is capped at ₹2,500, and rents and user charges are non-tax revenue.

st.3: Only 24 of the 28 Chief Ministers attended the 11th meeting.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: all 28 Chief Ministers attended, for the first time. Statement 4 is wrong: digital payments was not one of the 2015 sub-groups.

st.2: Currency in circulation includes notes only, not rupee coins or small coins.
st.3: 'Other deposits with the RBI' include the deposits of the Central and State Governments.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: currency in circulation includes notes, rupee coins and small coins. Statement 3 is wrong: 'other deposits' cover bodies such as the IMF and foreign central banks, not government deposits. Statement 4 is wrong: time deposits are part of M3, not M0.

st.3: Store of value and standard of deferred payments are contingent functions of money.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: basis of credit and liquidity are contingent functions. Statement 3 is wrong: store of value and standard of deferred payments are secondary functions.

st.3: The number of PSBs fell from 27 in 2017 to 12 in 2020.

x: All three statements are correct: the SBI associates and Bharatiya Mahila Bank merged in 2017, the 10-into-4 merger took effect on 1 April 2020, and PSBs fell from 27 to 12.

st.2: The RBI Act, 1934 was amended in 2018 to give inflation targeting a statutory basis.
st.1: The Monetary Policy Framework Agreement between the Government and the RBI was signed in February 2013.
st.4: Section 45ZN, on reporting after three consecutive quarters of breach, was first invoked in 2020.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the agreement was signed in February 2015. Statement 2 is wrong: the RBI Act was amended in 2016. Statement 3 is wrong: the five-yearly target is under Section 45ZA. Statement 4 is wrong: Section 45ZN was first invoked in 2022.

st.2: Inflation expectations have no effect on actual inflation.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: inflation expectations can feed actual inflation. Statement 3 is wrong: better storage and distribution eases supply shocks.

st.3: The 16th Finance Commission caps the States' fiscal deficit at 3.5% of GSDP for 2026-31.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: market borrowings, not Central loans, are the largest part of AP's debt. Statement 3 is wrong: the 16th Finance Commission's cap is 3% of GSDP.

st.1: Primary deficit is always greater than fiscal deficit.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: fiscal deficit exceeds primary deficit by the interest payments. Statement 2 is wrong: effective revenue deficit cannot exceed revenue deficit.

st.3: In FY 2025-26 up to January 2026 the rupee depreciated by about 5.4% against the US dollar.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: RBI intervention aims to curb excessive volatility, not to defend a fixed level of the rupee.

st.3: Rice-wheat expansion in Punjab, Telangana and MP (2015-2025) happened despite the absence of assured MSP procurement.
st.2: Wheat has the largest cropped area in India.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: rice, not wheat, has the largest cropped area. Statement 3 is wrong: the expansion was driven by assured MSP procurement. Statement 4 is wrong: shifting rice area to pulses would cut urea use.

st.2: The National Commission on Farmers was constituted on 18 November 2004 under Y.K. Alagh.
st.1: The National Commission on Agriculture (1970-76), chaired by M.S. Swaminathan, coined the term 'social forestry'.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the NCA was chaired by Nathu Ram Mirdha. Statement 2 is wrong: the NCF was headed by M.S. Swaminathan. Statement 3 is wrong: the NCF recommended MSP at C2 + 50%.

st.3: It has been under PM-KISAN since 2022-23.
st.2: It became a sub-mission of the National Food Security Mission from 2018-19.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: NMSA became a sub-mission of Krishonnati from 2018-19. Statement 3 is wrong: it has been under PM-RKVY since 2022-23. Statement 4 is wrong: e-NAM is not an NMSA component.

st.2: The Expert Group on Agricultural Indebtedness (2007) was chaired by C. Rangarajan.
st.1: The scheme for 10,000 FPOs (2020) has an outlay of Rs 8,665 crore.
st.3: The AP Microfinance Act, 2011 limits a borrower to five lenders, with a household cap of Rs 2 lakh.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the outlay is Rs 6,865 crore. Statement 2 is wrong: the Expert Group was chaired by R. Radhakrishna. Statement 3 is wrong: the limit is three lenders. Statement 4 is wrong: informal sources supplied 51.5% in the Guntur study.

st.1: They lend mainly to large farmers and agro-processing industries.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: RRBs lend mainly to small and marginal farmers, agricultural labourers and rural artisans. Statement 3 is wrong: RRBs are supervised by NABARD.

st.3: Equity grant is up to Rs 5,000 per farmer member.
st.1: It envisages one FPO per district.
st.4: Credit guarantee cover is available up to Rs 5 crore.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: it envisages one FPO per block. Statement 2 is wrong: CBBO handholding runs for five years. Statement 3 is wrong: the equity grant is up to Rs 2,000 per member. Statement 4 is wrong: credit guarantee is up to Rs 2 crore.

st.2: It is administered by the Bureau of Indian Standards under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs.
st.3: AGMARKNET, launched in 2010, is a portal for agricultural market prices.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 1937 Act is the Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act. Statement 2 is wrong: AGMARK is run by the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection under the Ministry of Agriculture. Statement 3 is wrong: AGMARKNET was launched in 2000.

st.1: Traders buy produce from farmers and resell it to consumers.
st.2: They operate through licensed commission agents.

x: Neither statement is correct: in Rythu Bazars farmers sell directly to consumers, and commission agents and traders are kept out.

st.4: Steel silos for foodgrain storage are being built only by the FCI with its own funds.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: target-based PSS procurement is capped at 25% of production. Statement 4 is wrong: steel silos are being built in PPP mode.

st.3: Banking, insurance and financial services form a strategic sector group.

x: All three statements are correct: atomic energy, space and defence form one strategic group, banking, insurance and financial services another, and non-strategic PSEs are to be privatised or closed.

st.2: Bokaro, India's fourth integrated plant, was set up during the Third Plan.

x: All three statements are correct: Bhilai (USSR) is the largest rail maker, Bhilai, Rourkela and Durgapur belong to the Second Plan, and Bokaro to the Third.

st.4: Pharmaceuticals were among the industries reserved for the public sector in 1991.
st.1: The New Industrial Policy, 1991 reserved 18 industries for the public sector.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 1991 policy reserved 8 industries (18 was the licensing list). Statement 2 is wrong: atomic energy and railway operations remain reserved. Statement 4 is wrong: pharmaceuticals were never on the reserved list.

st.4: The National Renewal Fund was set up in 1995.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: disinvestment in 1991-92 was of up to 20% in selected PSUs. Statement 4 is wrong: the National Renewal Fund was set up in 1992.

st.2: Reservation of items for the small-scale sector began in 1967.

x: All three statements are correct: the 1973 statement first listed core industries, small-scale reservation began in 1967, and it was fully removed in 2015.

st.4: In 2019 SEBI allowed a one-time restructuring of MSME loans without asset-classification downgrade.
st.3: The Liberalised Margin Money Scheme of June 1997 sought to reduce sickness in small-scale units.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the NRF was a social safety net for workers hit by restructuring, not modernisation capital. Statement 3 is wrong: the Liberalised Margin Money Scheme dates from June 1987. Statement 4 is wrong: the 2019 MSME restructuring was allowed by the RBI.

st.2: It earmarks 23.44 TMC for the drinking and industrial needs of Vijayawada.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 23.44 TMC is for Visakhapatnam. Statement 3 is wrong: the Right Main Canal carries Godavari water to the Krishna.

st.3: The Centre gave ₹25,000 crore special assistance for Amaravati (January 2026).
st.4: EAP inflow was ₹16,252 crore in 2025-26 RE.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Centre pays 90% of EAP cost. Statement 3 is wrong: Amaravati got ₹15,000 crore. Statement 4 is wrong: EAP inflow was ₹21,585 crore in 2025-26 RE (₹16,252 crore was 2024-25 RE).

st.1: e-NAM links 1,656 mandis in 18 States and 4 Union Territories.
st.2: Andhra Pradesh has 53 markets on e-NAM.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: e-NAM covers 23 States and 4 UTs. Statement 2 is wrong: AP has 33 markets on e-NAM. Statement 3 is wrong: each AP mandi received Rs 30 lakh.

st.2: Canals accounted for about 40% of the gross irrigated area, ahead of wells and tube wells together.
st.4: The State has about 9 lakh bore wells.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: wells and tube wells together (about 48%) lead canals (about 40%). Statement 3 is wrong: tanks are not the largest source. Statement 4 is wrong: AP has about 19 lakh bore wells.

st.1: Preferential access is limited to SC/ST entrepreneurs.

x: Neither statement is correct: preferential access covers women, SC/ST, BC and specially-abled entrepreneurs, and the additional 5% capital subsidy is not restricted to women.

st.2: Pochampally Ikat is a GI product of Telangana.

x: All three statements are correct: Bandar Laddu got GI in 2017, Pochampally Ikat belongs to Telangana, and Araku coffee and Banganapalle mango are AP GI products.

st.1: It came into force on 1 April 2024.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the policy came into force on 12 December 2024. Statement 3 is wrong: co-working spaces are planned in Tirupati, Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada.

st.3: Three of the eight MDGs were health goals, which were merged into SDG 3.

x: All three statements are correct: Agenda 2030 grew from the MDGs and Rio+20, is universal, and folds the three health MDGs into SDG 3.

st.3: It made India the first Asian nation to reach Mars orbit.

x: All three statements are correct: Mangalyaan was launched on PSLV-C25 in November 2013, entered Mars orbit on 24 September 2014, and made India the first Asian nation to do so.

st.2: Edwin Hubble's 1929 evidence of receding galaxies supported the expanding-universe idea.

x: All three statements are correct: Lemaitre proposed the expanding universe in 1927, Hubble's 1929 work supported it, and Hoyle, Bondi and Gold proposed the Steady State theory in 1948.

st.4: The tropical rainforest is the oldest and largest biome on Earth.
st.1: The Pacific Ocean has the largest share of continental shelf.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Atlantic has the largest share of continental shelf. Statement 3 is wrong: the shelf is narrow where mountains run parallel to the coast. Statement 4 is wrong: the deep sea below 200 m is the oldest and largest biome.

st.1: A heat wave in the plains is considered only when the maximum temperature reaches at least 37°C.
st.2: In coastal areas the threshold is 40°C.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the plains threshold is 40°C. Statement 2 is wrong: the coastal threshold is 37°C. Statement 4 is wrong: a severe heat wave in the plains is declared at an actual maximum of 47°C.

st.2: It increases as wind speed increases.

x: All three statements are correct: the Coriolis force deflects winds to the right in the Northern Hemisphere, rises with wind speed and is maximum at the poles.

st.3: Its sudden shift north of the Himalayas around June marks the onset of the monsoon.

x: All three statements are correct: the jet lies south of the Himalayas in winter, brings western disturbances, and its shift north in June marks the monsoon onset.

st.2: Groundwater holds about 68–70% of the Earth's fresh water.
st.1: Polar ice and glaciers hold a little over 30% of the Earth's fresh water.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: ice and glaciers hold about 68–70% of fresh water. Statement 2 is wrong: groundwater holds a little over 30%. Statement 3 is wrong: groundwater is a far larger store than lakes.

st.2: Uttar Pradesh does not share a border with Punjab.
